newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS - Dismal sales dampen Meralco net.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dismal sales dampen Meralco net.

text.p: The Manila Electric Co (Meralco), the Philippine's biggest power distributor, posted disappointing sales growth for the first quarter of 1997 and analysts said urgent steps were needed to boost demand.
"We were expecting sales growth of seven to eight percent at the worst. I think this is the lowest in years," said Cilette Liboro, research head at Orion-Squire Capital Inc.
"It seems that the slowdown in the property and the banking sectors is extending to the electricity sector as well," said Guoco Securities Philipines research head Saturnino Mejia.
Meralco president Manuel Lopez told stockholders he expects the company to post a 9.5 percent growth in sales this year.
Lisa Joson, research head at Amsteel Securities Philippines Inc said Meralco should start implementing its rate restructuring plans to spur demand among industrial customers.
Mejia said that while sales to residential and commercial customers seemed to be on track, there was a marked reduction in sales to industries during the first quarter.

The restructuring of rates allows Meralco to reflect the true cost of electricity by removing the subsidy provided by industries and at the same time awards efficient users of electricity with lower rates.
Lopez said he projected a 92 centavo per kwh reduction in rates to industries with the implementation of the new structure within the month.

"If they can implement restructuring then they can catch up. If National Power Corp can tap cheaper sources of fuel, then Meralco will benefit since it will have lower rates and they will be able to attract more buyers," said Orion-Squire's Liboro.
Meralco reported on Tuesday a net income of 1.1 billion pesos for the first three months of the year, an 8.3 percent hike from the previous year's 1.02 billion.
It's kilowatt-hour (kwh) sales was 5.4 percent higher at 4.2 billion kwhs from 3.98 billion kwhs.
Analysts said they were expecting an 8 to 10 percent increase in electricity sales.
"Electricity sales should be double-digit for the remaining quarters of the year for the company to meet its 9.5 percent full year target," said Joson.

Rosanna Tiosic, analyst at BPI Capital Corp, said Meralco may still benefit from a historical increase in demand for the second quarter due to the summer season and in the fourth quarter due to the Christmas holidays.
Other analysts said with the lower first quarter sales, Meralco may have to count on its non-core businesses to beef up its earnings for the year.
Meralco has a 51 percent stake in Rockwell Land Corp which is developing a 15-hectare land in Manila's financial district of Makati City into a mixed-use residential and commercial centre.
Analysts said the Philippine stock market, which on Tuesday suffered its biggest single-day drop in over two years, may be pushed down further by Meralco's performance.
"Meralco is the best GDP gauge and if it reported a slowdown then a lot of people would naturally assume that there may be some slowdown in the economy. That's the sentiment," Liboro added.
As a rule of thumb, a one percent increase in gross domestic product growth rate translates to a 1.5 to 1.7 percent growth in electricity demand.
-- MANILA NEWSROOM (63 2) 841 8939
